cell.label: History, physical, and respiratory assessment. Toxic or in severe respiratory distress?
Suction, assess respiratory status, and start O2 if SaO2 is consistently 91% or less. Medication trial desired?
Single-dose trial with epinephrine or albuterol. If improved, consider repeated inhalations.
Manage without medications (nasal suctioning, oxygen, monitoring).
Period of observation. Ready for discharge (RR <70, room air, oral feedings, family can provide care and monitoring, follow-up scheduled)?
Discharge home with parent education and primary care physician follow-up.
Monitor until ready for discharge, or admit. If admitted, consider cardiopulmonary monitoring, frequent respiratory and SaO2 checks, and suction before feeding and as needed.

footnotes.footnote: Adapted from Evidence Based Clinical Practice Guideline for Infants with Bronchiolitis. 2006 Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center. Page 7.
